source.text: Ἐγόγγυζον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι περὶ αὐτοῦ ὅτι εἶπεν· Ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ καταβὰς ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ, καὶ ἔλεγον· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν Ἰησοῦς ὁ υἱὸς Ἰωσήφ, οὗ ἡμεῖς οἴδαμεν τὸν πατέρα καὶ τὴν μητέρα;

records.literal_gloss: Were grumbling therefore the Jews about him because he said, "I am the bread the [one] having come down out of the heaven," \v 42 and they were saying, "Not this is Jesus the son of Joseph, of whom we know the father and the mother?

en.L: So the Jews were grumbling about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I am the bread that came down out of heaven," \v 42 and they were saying, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we ourselves know?
en.B: Then the Jews started grumbling about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had claimed, "I am the bread that came down from heaven." \v 42 They kept saying, "Surely this is Jesus, the son of Joseph? We know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} father and mother.
en.R: Then the Jewish people there began to grumble about Jesus, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, "I am the bread that came down from heaven." \v 42 They said, "This is Jesus, Joseph's son! We know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} father and mother.

es.L: Murmuraban, pues, los judíos acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque había dicho: «Yo soy el pan que bajó del cielo», \v 42 y decían: «¿No es este Jesús, el hijo de José, cuyo padre y madre nosotros conocemos?
es.B: Entonces los judíos comenzaron a murmurar contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, porque había dicho: «Yo soy el pan que bajó del cielo». \v 42 Decían: «¿No es este Jesús, el hijo de José? Nosotros conocemos a su padre y a su madre.
es.R: Entonces la gente judía que estaba allí comenzó a murmurar contra Jesús, porque había dicho: «Yo soy el pan que bajó del cielo». \v 42 Decían: «¡Este es Jesús, el hijo de José! Conocemos a su padre y a su madre.

decisions.choice: the Jews: the crowd in the synagogue at Capernaum, people of Galilee, not the authorities from Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The scene is the synagogue in Capernaum (6:59), and the speakers are the crowd that had eaten the loaves and crossed the lake to look for Jesus (6:22-25). What they say shows they are local people: they know Joseph, and Jesus's mother (verse 42). Nothing in the passage says that authorities had come from Jerusalem, as they do in 1:19 and Mark 7:1, though leaders of the local synagogue may be among them. John stops calling them "the crowd" and calls them "the Jews" at the point where they begin to reject what Jesus says. The word marks their response, not a difference of people: Jesus and his disciples are Jews too (4:9, 4:22).

decisions.choice: grumbling: the word for Israel's grumbling in the wilderness
alternatives: ordinary complaining, with no echo of Scripture
decisions.reason: The talk has been about the manna (6:31-32), and the verb Ἐγόγγυζον is the word the Greek Old Testament uses for Israel grumbling against Moses and against God over food in the wilderness, the very complaint that God answered by sending manna (Exodus 16:2-12; Numbers 11:1-6; 14:27). The crowd repeats what their ancestors did, and Jesus will say "your fathers ate the manna ... and died" (6:49). The tense pictures a muttering that went on among them (verse 43; compare 7:12 and 7:32), not one open protest.

decisions.choice: they judge his origin by the family they know
decisions.reason: The crowd reasons that a man whose parents they know cannot have come down from heaven. John lets the reader see the irony: they know where he comes from in one sense (7:27-28) but not in the sense that matters (8:14), for he is the Word who became flesh (1:14). Philip had already called him "son of Joseph" (1:45). The pronoun ἡμεῖς is stated, so it is emphatic: we, of all people, know his family. The passage does not say whether Joseph was still alive.

decisions.choice: the Jewish people there
decisions.reason: Readable names the group plainly, as the John term list asks: here the people of the synagogue in Capernaum (meaning decision m1). It does not say "leaders", because nothing in the scene points to the authorities.

decisions.choice: Surely this is Jesus ...? (B); This is Jesus ...! (R)
decisions.reason: The question begins with a negative that expects the answer yes. Balanced and Readable make that plain; Literal keeps the form of the question.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L, B); la gente judía que estaba allí (R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the crowd in the synagogue at Capernaum, not the authorities (meaning decision m1), so no level speaks of leaders.

decisions.choice: murmurar
decisions.reason: "Murmurar" is the word Spanish Bibles use for Israel's grumbling in the wilderness, so the echo of the manna story (meaning decision m2) stays visible at every level, here and in 6:43 and 6:61.

decisions.choice: ¿No es este ...? (L, B); ¡Este es ...! (R)
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer yes; Readable states it.

source.text: πῶς νῦν λέγει ὅτι Ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβέβηκα;

records.literal_gloss: How now does he say, "Out of the heaven I have come down"?"

en.L: How is it that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} now says, 'Out of heaven I have come down'?"
en.B: So what does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mean by saying now, 'I have come down from heaven'?"
en.R: So how can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} claim, 'I came down from heaven'?"

es.L: ¿Cómo, pues, dice ahora: “Del cielo he bajado”?».
es.B: ¿Qué quiere decir entonces con eso de: “He bajado del cielo”?».

decisions.choice: now: after all this, in the face of what we know
alternatives: now, at this moment, as opposed to earlier
decisions.reason: νῦν here has the force of "in these circumstances": given that they know his family, how can he say such a thing? It is an objection, not a question about the time when he began to say it.

decisions.choice: they quote his own words from 6:38
decisions.reason: The word ὅτι introduces a direct quotation, and the words that follow repeat what Jesus said in 6:38, with the same perfect tense: he came down and is now here. They have heard him exactly; their problem is not that they misheard but that they will not accept it.

decisions.choice: what does he mean by saying
decisions.reason: "How" here challenges the claim rather than asks for an explanation (meaning decision m1). Balanced puts it as a challenge in natural English; Readable uses "how can he claim".

decisions.choice: ¿Qué quiere decir entonces con eso de ...?
decisions.reason: As in English: "how" here challenges the claim (meaning decision m1). Spanish needs no pronoun for Jesus here.

source.text: ἀπεκρίθη Ἰησοῦς καὶ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Μὴ γογγύζετε μετ’ ἀλλήλων.

records.literal_gloss: Answered Jesus and said to them, "Not grumble with one another.

en.L: Jesus answered and said to them, "Do not grumble with one another.
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Stop your grumbling to one another.
en.R: Jesus told them, "Stop grumbling to each other.

es.L: Respondió Jesús y les dijo: «No {{plural_you:murmuren entre ustedes|murmuréis entre vosotros}}.
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «{{plural_you:Dejen de murmurar entre ustedes|Dejad de murmurar entre vosotros}}.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Dejen|Dejad}} de murmurar unos con otros.

decisions.choice: stop grumbling: the present command tells them to end what they are already doing
decisions.reason: γογγύζετε is a present command with a negative, which commonly forbids something already going on (compare 2:16 and 5:14). Their grumbling had begun in verse 41.

decisions.choice: with one another: talk among themselves, not words addressed to him
decisions.reason: The grumbling was among the crowd (verse 41 says it was "about him"). Jesus answers it all the same; John has already said that Jesus knew what was in people (2:24-25).

decisions.choice: answered and said (L); answered them (B)
decisions.reason: "Answered and said" is a common Greek way of introducing a reply; the second verb adds no separate action. Literal keeps both verbs, Balanced and Readable use one.

decisions.choice: Dejen de murmurar
decisions.reason: The present command tells them to stop what they are already doing (meaning decision m1). Every plural "you" in this passage is the ustedes / vosotros reader setting.

source.text: οὐδεὶς δύναται ἐλθεῖν πρός με ἐὰν μὴ ὁ πατὴρ ὁ πέμψας με ἑλκύσῃ αὐτόν, κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν ἐν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: No one is able to come to me if not the Father the [one] having sent me draws him, and I will raise up him in the last day.

en.L: No one is able to come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} unless the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} draws {{gender:them|him}}, and I will raise {{gender:them|him}} up on the last day.
en.B: Nobody can come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} unless the Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} draws {{gender:them|him}}. And on the last day I will raise {{gender:them|him}} up.
en.R: No one can come to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} unless the Father, who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, draws {{gender:them|him}} to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. And on the last day I will raise {{gender:them|him}} from the dead.

es.L: Nadie puede venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si el Padre que me envió no lo atrae, y yo lo resucitaré el último día.
es.B: Nadie puede venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si no lo atrae el Padre que me envió. Y yo lo resucitaré el último día.
es.R: Nadie puede venir a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} si el Padre, que me envió, no lo atrae hacia {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. Y el último día yo lo resucitaré.

decisions.choice: draws: the Father's own work that brings a person to Jesus
alternatives: only invites or attracts, leaving the rest to the person
decisions.reason: The verb ἑλκύσῃ is used of hauling a net (21:6, 21:11) and drawing a sword (18:10), so it is a strong word: the coming starts with the Father, not with the person. But in Scripture God draws people with love (Jeremiah 31:3, where the Greek Old Testament uses this verb), and Jesus says that when he is lifted up he will draw all people to himself (12:32). The next verse says how the drawing happens: people hear the Father and learn from him (6:45). The sentence does not say whether the drawing can be refused.

decisions.choice: God's initiative and human believing are both affirmed
decisions.reason: Jesus says here, as in 6:37 and 6:65, that coming to him depends on the Father. In the same chapter he calls people to believe and promises life to everyone who does (6:29, 6:35, 6:40, 6:47). The passage holds both together and does not explain how they fit; Christians have answered that question in different ways.

decisions.choice: the raising on the last day: bodily resurrection at the end of the age
decisions.reason: This is the third of four times the promise is made in this chapter (6:39, 6:40, 6:44, 6:54). The last day is the day of resurrection, as Martha understands it (11:24; compare 5:28-29). The one who believes already has eternal life (6:47); the raising on the last day completes it.

decisions.choice: {{gender:them|him}}
decisions.reason: "Him" stands for anyone at all who comes, man or woman, so the gender setting applies (as at 3:2).

decisions.choice: draws them to me; raise them from the dead
alternatives: draws them; raise them up (Literal, Balanced)
decisions.reason: Readable says where the Father draws people, to Jesus, which the start of the sentence implies, and what "raise up" means here (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: lo atrae, lo resucitaré: no gender setting
decisions.reason: After "nadie", Spanish refers back with the ordinary clitic "lo", which is general here, as at 6:40.

decisions.choice: hacia mí
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says where the Father draws people. Spanish "resucitar" already means raising from the dead.

source.text: ἔστιν γεγραμμένον ἐν τοῖς προφήταις· Καὶ ἔσονται πάντες διδακτοὶ θεοῦ· πᾶς ὁ ἀκούσας παρὰ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ μαθὼν ἔρχεται πρὸς ἐμέ.

records.literal_gloss: It is having been written in the prophets, "And they will be all taught of God." Everyone the [one] having heard from the Father and having learned comes to me.

en.L: It is written in the Prophets, 'And they will all be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard from the Father and has learned comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: In the Prophets it is written, 'They will all be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard the Father's teaching and learned it comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: The Prophets wrote, 'God will teach all of them.' Everyone who hears what the Father says and learns from it comes to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Está escrito en los Profetas: “Y serán todos enseñados por Dios”. Todo el que ha escuchado al Padre y ha aprendido viene a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: En los Profetas está escrito: “Todos serán enseñados por Dios”. Todo el que ha escuchado la enseñanza del Padre y la ha aprendido viene a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Los Profetas escribieron: “Dios les enseñará a todos”. Todo el que escucha lo que dice el Padre y aprende de ello viene a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

decisions.choice: Isaiah 54:13: all will be taught by God
decisions.reason: The words come from Isaiah 54:13, a promise to restored Jerusalem that all her children will be taught by the Lord. The Hebrew has the divine name there; the Greek translation of Isaiah has "God", and so does John. Jeremiah 31:33-34 makes the same promise for the new covenant, when all will know the Lord. Isaiah says "your children"; Jesus's "all" leaves out the limit.

decisions.choice: the Prophets: a section of Scripture
alternatives: a group of people, the prophets
decisions.reason: Jews of the time spoke of the Scriptures as the Law and the Prophets (Luke 24:44; Acts 13:15). "In the Prophets" names the part of Scripture where the words stand, the way 1:45 speaks of what Moses wrote "in the Law".

decisions.choice: the Father draws people by teaching them
decisions.reason: This sentence explains the drawing of 6:44. Those whom God teaches, who have heard from the Father and learned, come to Jesus. Coming to Jesus is the sign that someone has heard the Father; refusing him shows the opposite (5:37-38; 8:47).

decisions.choice: taught by God
decisions.reason: The Greek has "God", so every level keeps it, though the Hebrew of Isaiah has the divine name (meaning decision m1). "Of God" in the gloss is the Greek form; "by God" is the English sense. Readable says "God will teach".

decisions.choice: the Prophets, with a capital
decisions.reason: A capital shows that this names a part of Scripture (meaning decision m2), not the prophets as people.

decisions.choice: los Profetas, with a capital
decisions.reason: As in English: names a part of Scripture (meaning decision m2).

source.text: οὐχ ὅτι τὸν πατέρα ἑώρακέν τις εἰ μὴ ὁ ὢν παρὰ τοῦ θεοῦ, οὗτος ἑώρακεν τὸν πατέρα.

records.literal_gloss: Not that the Father has seen anyone, if not the [one] being from the God, this [one] has seen the Father.

en.L: Not that anyone has seen the Father, except the one who is from God: this one has seen the Father.
en.B: This does not mean that anyone has seen the Father. Only the one who has come from God has seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: I do not mean that anyone has seen the Father. The only one who has seen the Father is the one who comes from God.

es.L: No que alguien haya visto al Padre, sino el que es de Dios; este ha visto al Padre.
es.B: Esto no quiere decir que alguien haya visto al Padre. Solo el que ha venido de Dios lo ha visto.
es.R: No quiero decir que alguien haya visto al Padre. El único que ha visto al Padre es el que viene de Dios.

decisions.choice: not that: a correction, so verse 45 is not misread
decisions.reason: οὐχ ὅτι heads off a wrong conclusion. Hearing and learning from the Father (6:45) does not mean that anyone sees the Father directly. People hear the Father through the one he has sent.

decisions.choice: the one from God is Jesus himself, the only one who has seen the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of himself in the third person, as he often does (3:13; 5:19). The sentence repeats the claim of 1:18: no one has ever seen God, and the only Son has made him known. Compare 3:11, 3:32 and 7:29, "I know him, because I am from him".

decisions.choice: from God: coming from God's own presence
alternatives: sent by God, as a prophet is sent
decisions.reason: τοῦ with the genitive means "from beside". The same phrase can be used of a messenger such as John the Baptist (1:6). Here, though, the one who is from God is the one who has seen the Father, so it means coming from God's presence, as in 16:27-28 and 17:8.

decisions.choice: has come from God (B); comes from God (R)
decisions.reason: "Is from God" can sound like a statement about birthplace or about character; "has come from" makes the movement plain, as in 16:28.

decisions.choice: el que ha venido de Dios (B); el que viene de Dios (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: makes the movement plain (meaning decision m3).

source.text: ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ὁ πιστεύων ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον.

records.literal_gloss: Truly truly I say to you, the [one] believing has life eternal.

en.L: Truly, truly I say to you, the one who believes has eternal life.
en.B: Truly, truly, I tell you, anyone who believes has eternal life.
en.R: I tell you the truth: anyone who believes has eternal life already.

es.L: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: el que cree tiene vida eterna.
es.B: En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que quien cree tiene vida eterna.
es.R: {{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: quien cree ya tiene vida eterna.

decisions.choice: the one who believes, with no object (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the one who believes in me (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "in me" after "believes". The earliest papyri and the major early manuscripts do not have it, and the SBLGNT follows them; the addition looks like a natural way of filling out the sense. The meaning is the same either way, since the whole passage is about believing in Jesus (6:29, 6:35, 6:40). A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: has: eternal life is held now
alternatives: will have, only in the future
decisions.reason: The verb is present. Eternal life begins when a person believes (3:36; 5:24), and the raising on the last day (6:44) completes it.

decisions.choice: Truly, truly I say to you (L); Truly, truly, I tell you (B); I tell you the truth (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide rendering for John (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 6:53 as well.

decisions.choice: already
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain that the present tense means now (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: En verdad, en verdad les digo (L, B); Les digo la verdad (R)
decisions.reason: The book-wide Spanish rendering (see 1:51), recorded once in this passage; it covers 6:53 as well.

decisions.choice: ya
decisions.reason: As in English: the present tense means now (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος τῆς ζωῆς·

records.literal_gloss: I am the bread of the life;

en.L: I am the bread of life.
en.B: I am the bread of life.
en.R: I am the bread that gives life.

es.L: Yo soy el pan de vida.
es.B: Yo soy el pan de vida.
es.R: Yo soy el pan que da vida.

decisions.choice: bread of life: the bread that gives life
decisions.reason: The bread is described by what it does: it gives life to the world (6:33) and those who eat it will not die (6:50). In 6:51 Jesus also calls it "living bread". The saying repeats 6:35 and begins the comparison with the manna in the next sentences.

decisions.choice: I am, with a predicate: an ordinary statement, the first of John's images
alternatives: an echo of the divine name
decisions.reason: Here "I am" is followed by what he is, so it is an ordinary statement of identity, as in 8:12 (the light of the world) and 10:11 (the good shepherd). The uses without a predicate, which echo God's name, come later (8:24, 8:58).

decisions.choice: the bread that gives life
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "of life" means (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: el pan que da vida
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable says what "de vida" means (meaning decision m1).

source.text: οἱ πατέρες ὑμῶν ἔφαγον ἐν τῇ ἐρήμῳ τὸ μάννα καὶ ἀπέθανον·

records.literal_gloss: The fathers of you ate in the wilderness the manna and died;

en.L: Your fathers ate in the wilderness the manna, and they died.
en.B: Your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} ate the manna in the wilderness, and yet they died.
en.R: Your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} ate manna in the wilderness, but they still died.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sus padres|Vuestros padres}} comieron en el desierto el maná, y murieron.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sus antepasados|Vuestros antepasados}} comieron el maná en el desierto, y aun así murieron.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sus antepasados|Vuestros antepasados}} comieron maná en el desierto, pero de todos modos murieron.

decisions.choice: the manna: the food God gave Israel in the wilderness
decisions.reason: God gave the manna each morning for forty years (Exodus 16; Numbers 11:7-9). The crowd had quoted Psalm 78:24, "he gave them bread from heaven to eat" (6:31). That generation died in the wilderness (Numbers 14:29-35).

decisions.choice: fathers: ancestors, men and women
decisions.reason: πατέρες is the usual word for forebears, as in 4:20. The crowd had said "our fathers" (6:31); Jesus answers "your fathers", taking up their own claim. He is not setting himself apart from Israel.

decisions.choice: died: bodily death, which the manna could not prevent
decisions.reason: The manna kept people alive for a day at a time but did not stop them dying. That is the contrast with the bread from heaven that Jesus is, which gives life that does not end (verses 50-51).

decisions.choice: Your {{gender:ancestors|fathers}}
decisions.reason: The word means the people of that generation, men and women (meaning decision m2), so the gender setting applies. Literal keeps "fathers", the form of the Greek.

decisions.choice: antepasados, no gender setting (B, R); padres (L)
decisions.reason: The word means forebears, men and women (meaning decision m2). Spanish "antepasados" already includes both, so Balanced and Readable need no gender setting, as at 4:20 and 6:31; Literal keeps "padres".

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβαίνων ἵνα τις ἐξ αὐτοῦ φάγῃ καὶ μὴ ἀποθάνῃ·

records.literal_gloss: This is the bread the [one] out of the heaven coming down, so that anyone of it may eat and not die;

en.L: This is the bread that comes down out of heaven, so that anyone may eat of it and not die.
en.B: Here, by contrast, is bread coming down from heaven: whoever eats it will not die.
en.R: But this bread comes down from heaven. Anyone who eats it will not die.

es.L: Este es el pan que baja del cielo, para que uno coma de él y no muera.
es.B: Este, en cambio, es el pan que baja del cielo: quien lo come no morirá.
es.R: Pero este pan baja del cielo. Quien lo coma no morirá.

decisions.choice: this: the bread that Jesus is, coming down from heaven
decisions.reason: "This" points back to Jesus's words "I am the bread of life" (6:48). Set beside verse 49, it marks a contrast with the manna. The present participle speaks of the bread as coming down, what it is and does (compare 6:33).

decisions.choice: not die: not lose life in the full sense, though the body dies
decisions.reason: Those who eat the manna died (verse 49), and believers die too. Jesus's promise is that death does not end the life he gives: "even if they die, they will live" (11:25-26), and he will raise them on the last day (6:54).

decisions.choice: Here, by contrast (B); But (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek sets this sentence directly beside verse 49 with no linking word. Balanced and Readable add a word to show the contrast between the manna and this bread (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: en cambio (B); Pero (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the contrast with verse 49.

source.text: ἐγώ εἰμι ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ζῶν ὁ ἐκ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς· ἐάν τις φάγῃ ἐκ τούτου τοῦ ἄρτου ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα, καὶ ὁ ἄρτος δὲ ὃν ἐγὼ δώσω ἡ σάρξ μού ἐστιν ὑπὲρ τῆς τοῦ κόσμου ζωῆς.

records.literal_gloss: I am the bread the living the [one] out of the heaven having come down; if anyone eats of this the bread he will live into the age, and the bread also which I will give the flesh of me is, for the of the world life.

en.L: I am the living bread that came down out of heaven; if anyone eats of this bread, {{gender:they|he}} will live forever; and the bread that I will give is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh, for the life of the world.
en.B: I am the living bread, come down from heaven. If anyone eats this bread, {{gender:they|he}} will live forever. The bread I will give is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh, and I give it so that the world may have life.
en.R: I am the bread that is alive, the bread that came down from heaven. Anyone who eats this bread will live forever. The bread I will give is {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh. I give it for the world, so that the world can have life.

es.L: Yo soy el pan vivo que bajó del cielo; si alguien come de este pan, vivirá para siempre; y el pan que yo daré es mi carne, por la vida del mundo».
es.B: Yo soy el pan vivo que bajó del cielo. Si alguien come de este pan, vivirá para siempre. El pan que yo daré es mi carne, y la doy para que el mundo tenga vida».
es.R: Yo soy el pan que está vivo, el pan que bajó del cielo. Quien come de este pan vivirá para siempre. El pan que yo daré es mi carne. La doy por el mundo, para que el mundo tenga vida».

decisions.choice: living: alive and giving life
decisions.reason: ζῶν means alive. As with the "living water" of 4:10, the bread is not only alive itself but gives life to those who receive it (6:57).

decisions.choice: flesh: his human body and life, given up in death
alternatives: body, as in the words at the Last Supper
decisions.reason: σάρξ recalls 1:14, "the Word became flesh": the bread is the human life of the Son of God. The future "I will give" looks ahead to his death. The other Gospels' account of the Last Supper uses a different word, "body" (Mark 14:22), and John keeps his own word all through this passage (6:51-56).

decisions.choice: for: on behalf of, for the sake of the world's life
decisions.reason: In John ὑπὲρ with the genitive is used again and again of Jesus's death for others: the good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep (10:11, 10:15), one man dies for the people (11:50-52; 18:14), a man lays down his life for his friends (15:13). Here the gift of his flesh is for the life of the world, the people God loved and sent his Son to save (3:16-17).

decisions.choice: the bread that I will give is my flesh, for the life of the world (SBLGNT)
alternatives: the bread that I will give is my flesh, which I will give for the life of the world (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts repeat "which I will give" before "for the life of the world", which smooths the sentence. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text, which the SBLGNT follows. The meaning does not change. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: will live forever
decisions.reason: "Into the age" is a Greek idiom for "forever"; English has no such phrase, so even Literal says "forever".

decisions.choice: and I give it so that the world may have life (B); I give it for the world, so that the world can have life (R)
alternatives: for the life of the world (Literal)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable spell out the compressed phrase as a clause (meaning decision m3), so that "for" is not read as "in exchange for". Every level keeps "flesh" rather than "body" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: la doy para que el mundo tenga vida
decisions.reason: As in English: spells out the compressed phrase (meaning decision m3). Spanish "si alguien come ... vivirá" needs no pronoun, so no gender setting.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes at the end of this verse
decisions.reason: Jesus's words end here and the crowd answers in 6:52. (The English leaves this quotation open.)

source.text: Ἐμάχοντο οὖν πρὸς ἀλλήλους οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι λέγοντες· Πῶς δύναται οὗτος ἡμῖν δοῦναι τὴν σάρκα αὐτοῦ φαγεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: Were fighting therefore with one another the Jews, saying, "How is able this [one] to us to give the flesh of him to eat?"

en.L: So the Jews were fighting with one another, saying, "How is this [man] able to give us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh to eat?"
en.B: At this the Jews began to quarrel fiercely among themselves. "How can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh to eat?" they said.
en.R: Then the Jewish people there started arguing with each other. "This man wants to give us {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flesh to eat?" they said. "How could {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} do that?"

es.L: Los judíos, pues, discutían entre sí, diciendo: «¿Cómo puede este darnos a comer su carne?».
es.B: Entonces los judíos se pusieron a discutir acaloradamente entre ellos: «¿Cómo puede {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} darnos a comer su carne?», decían.
es.R: Entonces la gente judía que estaba allí comenzó a discutir. «¿Este hombre quiere darnos a comer su carne?», decían. «¿Cómo podría hacer eso?».

decisions.choice: the Jews: the same crowd as in 6:41, the people in the synagogue at Capernaum
decisions.reason: The group is the one that grumbled in verse 41, in the same place (6:59). Nothing shows that the authorities are in view; see the note at 6:41.

decisions.choice: were fighting: a sharp dispute, worse than the grumbling
decisions.reason: Ἐμάχοντο means to fight or quarrel; here it is a fight with words. The muttering of verse 41 has become an open quarrel. "With one another" suggests they did not all agree, as the crowds are divided over Jesus in 7:43, 9:16 and 10:19.

decisions.choice: they take his words in the most physical sense, and Jesus does not soften them
decisions.reason: As Nicodemus did with being born again (3:4) and the Samaritan woman with living water (4:11), the hearers take Jesus's words at the most physical level. Here Jesus does not explain the saying away; he repeats it more strongly (6:53-56). What the words do mean is taken up at 6:53 and 6:63.

decisions.choice: the Jewish people there
decisions.reason: As at 6:41, Readable names the group plainly (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: he (B); This man (R)
decisions.reason: "This one" can sound dismissive in Greek. Balanced uses a simple pronoun; Readable keeps "this man" and splits the question in two to keep it short.

decisions.choice: la gente judía que estaba allí
decisions.reason: As at 6:41: the crowd in the synagogue (meaning decision m1).

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν αὐτοῖς ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἀμὴν ἀμὴν λέγω ὑμῖν, ἐὰν μὴ φάγητε τὴν σάρκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου καὶ πίητε αὐτοῦ τὸ αἷμα, οὐκ ἔχετε ζωὴν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore to them the Jesus, "Truly truly I say to you, if not you eat the flesh of the Son of the Man and drink of him the blood, not you have life in yourselves.

en.L: So Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly I say to you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, you do not have life in yourselves.
en.B: Jesus answered them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, if you do not eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood, there is no life in you.
en.R: Jesus told them, "I tell you the truth: you must eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blood. If you do not, you have no life in you.

es.L: Jesús, pues, les dijo: «En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo: si no {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} la carne del Hijo del Hombre y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}} su sangre, no {{plural_you:tienen vida en ustedes|tenéis vida en vosotros}} mismos.
es.B: Jesús les respondió: «En verdad, en verdad {{plural_you:les|os}} digo que si no {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} la carne del Hijo del Hombre y no {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}} su sangre, no hay vida en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.
es.R: Jesús les dijo: «{{plural_you:Les|Os}} digo la verdad: {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} que comer la carne del Hijo del Hombre y beber su sangre. Si no lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}, no {{plural_you:tienen|tenéis}} vida en {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}.

decisions.choice: eating his flesh and drinking his blood: what the words say, and the main ways they have been read
decisions.reason: Jesus restates his saying more starkly, adding the blood. The words have been read in two main ways, which are often held together. Some read them as speaking of the Lord's Supper, where believers eat the bread and drink the cup that Jesus gave as his body and blood (Mark 14:22-24; 1 Corinthians 10:16; 11:23-26). Others read them as a vivid picture of believing in Jesus and receiving the life he gives through his death, since the same promises are made to the one who believes (6:35, 6:40, 6:47) and Jesus later says that his words are spirit and life (6:63). The text does not settle the question between these readings, and the translation gives the words as they stand.

decisions.choice: drinking blood was forbidden in the Law, so the saying would shock
decisions.reason: God's law forbade eating meat with the blood in it, because the life is in the blood (Genesis 9:4; Leviticus 17:10-14; compare Acts 15:20). To hear of drinking anyone's blood would have been deeply offensive to Jewish listeners, which helps explain the reaction of many disciples in 6:60-66. Flesh and blood named separately also suggest a death in which the blood is shed.

decisions.choice: life in yourselves: life of your own, coming from him
decisions.reason: The phrase recalls 5:26: the Father has life in himself and has given the Son to have life in himself. Without receiving the Son, people have no such life in them. "Life" here is the eternal life of 6:54.

decisions.choice: if you do not ... there is no life in you (B); you must ... If you do not, you have no life in you (R)
alternatives: unless you ... you do not have life in yourselves (Literal)
decisions.reason: Readable turns the condition into a plain command followed by its consequence, to keep the sentences short. Both levels say "in you" for "in yourselves", which sounds natural and means the same.

decisions.choice: tienen que ... Si no lo hacen
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable turns the condition into a plain statement followed by its consequence.

source.text: ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἔχει ζωὴν αἰώνιον, κἀγὼ ἀναστήσω αὐτὸν τῇ ἐσχάτῃ ἡμέρᾳ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] chewing of me the flesh and drinking of me the blood has life eternal, and I will raise up him in the last day.

en.L: The one who feeds on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh and drinks {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood has eternal life, and I will raise {{gender:them|him}} up on the last day.
en.B: Anyone who eats {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh and drinks {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood has eternal life, and on the last day I will raise {{gender:them|him}} up.
en.R: Those who eat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh and drink {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood have eternal life. On the last day I will raise them from the dead.

es.L: El que se alimenta de mi carne y bebe mi sangre tiene vida eterna, y yo lo resucitaré el último día.
es.B: Quien come mi carne y bebe mi sangre tiene vida eterna, y yo lo resucitaré el último día.
es.R: Los que comen mi carne y beben mi sangre tienen vida eterna. Yo los resucitaré el último día.

decisions.choice: eats: a change of verb that most likely means no more than "eat"
alternatives: chew or munch, stressing physical eating
decisions.reason: Up to verse 53 the word for eating is the one used in φάγῃ and φάγητε. From here on (6:54, 6:56, 6:57, 6:58) it is τρώγων. In older Greek this verb meant to munch or chew, and some read the change as stressing real eating. But in New Testament times it was often simply "eat" (Matthew 24:38), and John never uses the present tense of the other verb: every present-tense "eat" in his Gospel is this one, including 13:18, where Jesus quotes Psalm 41:9, "the one who eats my bread". Here all four uses are present participles, so the change most likely comes from the tense.

decisions.choice: the same promises as for believing in 6:40
decisions.reason: This verse matches 6:40 almost clause for clause. There everyone who looks to the Son and believes in him has eternal life and will be raised on the last day; here it is the one who eats his flesh and drinks his blood. Some take the parallel to show that eating and drinking are a picture of believing; others take it to mean that believing is expressed in sharing the Lord's Supper. See the note at 6:53.

decisions.choice: eats and drinks: present tense, an ongoing feeding
decisions.reason: In 6:50-53 the verbs were aorist, looking at eating as a whole. Here the present participles describe the one who keeps feeding on him, as "the one who believes" (6:47) describes a person who goes on believing.

decisions.choice: feeds on (L); eats (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal uses a different English verb wherever the Greek changes verb (6:54-58), so readers can see the change; "chews" would overstate it (meaning decision m1). Balanced and Readable say "eat", as the verb most likely means.

decisions.choice: raise them from the dead
decisions.reason: As at 6:44, Readable says what the raising is. It uses the plural "those who", which needs no gender setting.

decisions.choice: se alimenta de (L); come (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal uses a different verb wherever the Greek changes verb (6:54-58), so readers can see the change (meaning decision m1); "masticar" would overstate it.

source.text: ἡ γὰρ σάρξ μου ἀληθής ἐστι βρῶσις, καὶ τὸ αἷμά μου ἀληθής ἐστι πόσις.

records.literal_gloss: The for flesh of me true is food, and the blood of me true is drink.

en.L: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh is food that is true, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood is drink that is true.
en.B: For {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh is genuine food, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood is genuine drink.
en.R: My flesh is food in the fullest sense, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood is drink in the fullest sense.

es.L: Porque mi carne es comida verdadera, y mi sangre es bebida verdadera.
es.B: Porque mi carne es comida de verdad, y mi sangre es bebida de verdad.
es.R: Mi carne es comida en el sentido más pleno, y mi sangre es bebida en el sentido más pleno.

decisions.choice: true (an adjective) twice (SBLGNT)
alternatives: truly (an adverb): my flesh truly is food, and my blood truly is drink (some manuscripts)
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT reads ἀληθής, "true", following early manuscripts. Other manuscripts, including many later ones, read ἀληθῶς, "truly": "my flesh truly is food". The difference is small: one says what kind of food it is, the other insists that it really is food. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: true: genuine food, that does what food is for
decisions.reason: The word means real or genuine. The manna fed people only for a time, and they died (6:49); the food Jesus gives lasts and gives eternal life (6:27). It is food that fully does what food is meant to do. The sentence does not by itself say how the eating takes place; see the note at 6:53.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for verse 54
decisions.reason: The sentence explains why the one who eats and drinks has eternal life: because this is the real food and drink.

decisions.choice: genuine (B); in the fullest sense (R)
decisions.reason: "True food" can sound as if other food were false. Balanced uses "genuine", and Readable explains the sense (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: de verdad (B); en el sentido más pleno (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "comida verdadera" could sound as if other food were false (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ὁ τρώγων μου τὴν σάρκα καὶ πίνων μου τὸ αἷμα ἐν ἐμοὶ μένει κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: The [one] chewing of me the flesh and drinking of me the blood in me remains and I in him.

en.L: The one who feeds on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh and drinks {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood remains in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I in {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: Anyone who eats {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh and drinks {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood remains in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I remain in {{gender:them|him}}.
en.R: Those who eat {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} flesh and drink {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} blood remain in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I remain in them.

es.L: El que se alimenta de mi carne y bebe mi sangre permanece en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y yo en {{gender:esa persona|él}}.
es.B: Quien come mi carne y bebe mi sangre permanece en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y yo permanezco en {{gender:esa persona|él}}.
es.R: Los que comen mi carne y beben mi sangre permanecen en {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y yo permanezco en ellos.

decisions.choice: remains: a lasting, living union
decisions.reason: μένει is a favorite word of John, used for staying in a place (1:38-39) and for a lasting union with Jesus. This is the first time in the Gospel that it describes the bond between Jesus and those who are his. The theme returns in the image of the vine (15:4-10) and in 1 John 3:24 and 4:13-16.

decisions.choice: a mutual indwelling: they in him and he in them
decisions.reason: The result of eating and drinking here is that the person remains in Jesus and Jesus in them. The same two-way union is described elsewhere in terms of keeping his words and his love (15:4-10; 1 John 3:24), and it mirrors the union of the Father and the Son (14:10-11, 14:20; 17:21-23). On the main lines of reading the eating and drinking, see the note at 6:53.

decisions.choice: the sentence ends here (SBLGNT)
alternatives: a longer text in one manuscript, continuing with words about the Father and the Son and about receiving the body of the Son of Man
decisions.reason: One early manuscript, Codex Bezae, adds a further sentence at this point. No other early manuscript has it, and the SBLGNT does not. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: and I remain in them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable repeat the verb, which the Greek leaves understood. Literal has the shorter form. The gender setting applies where the singular "him" means anyone; Readable's plural needs none.

decisions.choice: permanecer
decisions.reason: John's word for a lasting union, as in 1:32-33 and 5:38.

decisions.choice: {{gender:esa persona|él}}
decisions.reason: The stressed "él" here means the believer, anyone at all, so it takes the gender setting, with the traditional "él" one tap away. Readable uses the plural.

source.text: καθὼς ἀπέστειλέν με ὁ ζῶν πατὴρ κἀγὼ ζῶ διὰ τὸν πατέρα, καὶ ὁ τρώγων με κἀκεῖνος ζήσει δι’ ἐμέ.

records.literal_gloss: Just as sent me the living Father and I live because of the Father, also the [one] chewing me, that [one] also will live because of me.

en.L: Just as the living Father sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I live because of the Father, so also the one who feeds on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, that one also will live because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: The living Father sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I live because of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; in the same way, anyone who feeds on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will live because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: The Father who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is alive, and I have life from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. In the same way, anyone who feeds on {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} will have life from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Así como me envió el Padre que vive, y yo vivo por el Padre, también el que se alimenta de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, ese también vivirá por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: El Padre que vive me envió, y yo vivo por {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; de la misma manera, el que se alimenta de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} vivirá por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: El Padre que me envió está vivo, y yo tengo vida gracias a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. De la misma manera, el que se alimenta de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} tendrá vida gracias a {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

decisions.choice: the living Father: God, who has life in himself
decisions.reason: Only here does Jesus say "the living Father". It echoes the Old Testament's "living God" (Deuteronomy 5:26; Psalm 42:2; Hosea 1:10), the God who has life in himself and gives it (5:26). Life passes from the Father to the Son, and from the Son to those who feed on him.

decisions.choice: because of: the Father is the source of the Son's life, and the Son of the believer's
alternatives: for the sake of: I live for the Father, and they will live for me
decisions.reason: διὰ with the accusative usually gives the cause or ground: the Son lives because of the Father, and the one who feeds on him will live because of him. Some take it as the goal (living for the sake of), but the chain of life in this sentence and in 5:26 points to the source.

decisions.choice: feeds on me: what is received is Jesus himself
decisions.reason: Here the object is no longer "my flesh" but "me". Whatever the eating means, what is received is the person of Jesus, the living one. This does not by itself settle how the earlier verses should be read; see the note at 6:53.

decisions.choice: feeds on me
decisions.reason: With a person as its object, "eats" sounds strange in English, so every level says "feeds on" here. Readable says "have life from" for "live because of" (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: se alimenta de mí
decisions.reason: As in English: with a person as its object, every level says "se alimenta de" here (meaning decision m3).

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ ἄρτος ὁ ἐξ οὐρανοῦ καταβάς, οὐ καθὼς ἔφαγον οἱ πατέρες καὶ ἀπέθανον· ὁ τρώγων τοῦτον τὸν ἄρτον ζήσει εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα.

records.literal_gloss: This is the bread the [one] out of heaven having come down, not as ate the fathers and died; the [one] chewing this the bread will live into the age.

en.L: This is the bread that came down out of heaven, not as the fathers ate and died; the one who feeds on this bread will live forever.
en.B: This, then, is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not like the food the {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} ate, for they died; anyone who eats this bread will live forever.
en.R: So this is the bread that came down from heaven. It is not like the manna the {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} ate. They died, but anyone who eats this bread will live forever.

es.L: Este es el pan que bajó del cielo; no como [el que] comieron los padres, y murieron; el que se alimenta de este pan vivirá para siempre».
es.B: Este es, pues, el pan que bajó del cielo. No es como lo que comieron los antepasados, que murieron; quien come este pan vivirá para siempre».
es.R: Así que este es el pan que bajó del cielo. No es como el maná que comieron los antepasados. Ellos murieron, pero quien come este pan vivirá para siempre».

decisions.choice: the fathers ate (SBLGNT)
alternatives: your fathers ate the manna (many later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts read "your fathers ate the manna", filling out the phrase from 6:31 and 6:49. The earliest manuscripts have the shorter text, which the SBLGNT follows. The meaning is the same. A reviewer should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: not as the fathers ate: unlike the bread the fathers ate, who died anyway
decisions.reason: The comparison is compressed: the bread from heaven is not like what the ancestors ate in the wilderness, for they ate and still died (6:49).

decisions.choice: the summary of the teaching that began at 6:31
decisions.reason: The sentence draws together the whole discussion: the crowd's words about bread from heaven (6:31), Jesus's claim to be that bread (6:35, 6:41, 6:48-51), the contrast with the manna (6:49-50), and the promise of life forever (6:51). "This bread" and "my flesh" are one subject: the verb for eating used with his flesh (6:54-57) is now used with the bread.

decisions.choice: the food the {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} ate (B); the manna the {{gender:ancestors|fathers}} ate (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable supply what the ancestors ate, since English cannot leave it out; Readable names the manna, as in 6:49. The gender setting applies as at 6:49. Literal says "feeds on" here, as at 6:54.

decisions.choice: lo que comieron (B); el maná que comieron (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: supplies what the ancestors ate. "Antepasados" needs no gender setting (see 6:49).

decisions.choice: the quotation closes at the end of this verse
decisions.reason: Jesus's words end here, and 6:59 is the narrator's. (The English leaves this quotation open.)

source.text: ταῦτα εἶπεν ἐν συναγωγῇ διδάσκων ἐν Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: These things he said in synagogue teaching in Capernaum.

en.L: These things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said in [the] synagogue, teaching in Capernaum.
en.B: All this {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} taught in the synagogue in Capernaum.
en.R: Jesus said all this while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching in the synagogue, the Jewish meeting house in Capernaum.

es.L: Estas cosas dijo en la sinagoga, enseñando en Capernaúm.
es.B: Todo esto lo dijo mientras enseñaba en la sinagoga de Capernaúm.
es.R: Jesús dijo todo esto mientras enseñaba en la sinagoga, el lugar de reunión de los judíos en Capernaúm.

decisions.choice: in synagogue: in the synagogue, during a gathering
alternatives: in an assembly (the meeting rather than the building)
decisions.reason: συναγωγῇ has no article, as is common in set phrases about places (compare 18:20). It can mean the building or the gathering held in it. Capernaum had a synagogue, where Jesus taught on the Sabbath (Mark 1:21; Luke 7:5), and the phrase most likely means that one.

decisions.choice: the synagogue: the place where Jews gathered to hear Scripture read and taught
decisions.reason: Jews met in the synagogue on the Sabbath to read and explain the Law and the Prophets, and a visiting teacher could be invited to speak (Luke 4:16-21; Acts 13:15). This explains why Jesus quotes and explains Scripture (6:31, 6:45).

decisions.choice: these things: the teaching from 6:26 onward
decisions.reason: The note of place closes the whole discussion with the crowd that found Jesus in Capernaum (6:24-25). It also shows that the hearers of 6:41 and 6:52 were people of the synagogue there.

decisions.choice: [the] synagogue (L); the synagogue (B, R); the Jewish meeting house (R)
decisions.reason: English needs an article (meaning decision m1). Readable briefly explains the word "synagogue", which some readers may not know (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: la sinagoga (L); el lugar de reunión de los judíos (R)
decisions.reason: Spanish needs the article after the preposition, so Literal gives it without brackets. Readable explains the word (meaning decision m2).
